requirement_text.REQ-395:
Deploy SwiftRoute's sequential high-value shipment-approval process definition as a live, browsable definition on a real tenant, with ops-manager/CEO actors that can actually sign in.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY: The sequential HUMAN_TASK chain this scenario describes (dispatcher submits, ops manager reviews, and when declared_value > 500 the CEO must additionally co-sign before shipment releases) is a real, provable capability of Letflow.Engine: test/fixtures/simulation/swiftroute/process_route_approval.yaml ('Shipment Approval') is exactly this graph, and test/letflow/simulation/req206_swiftroute_test.exs already proves it end-to-end against a real Engine.create/2 call (REQ-206, done 2026-09-01). So the ENGINE capability is not the gap.

What genuinely does not exist: this definition DEPLOYED anywhere a human (or an agent driving a real browser) could reach on https://qa.bizdala.com today. process_route_approval.yaml is consumed only as an in-memory fixture by Letflow.Simulation.Runner.run/1 during automated test/CI runs -- it is provisioned fresh (and torn down) inside that harness, never persisted as a live ProcessDefinition row for a real swiftroute tenant a person could open in the process-definition list screen or submit an instance against via the ordinary API/GUI.

SEPARATELY, this scenario's actors (dispatcher Lena, ops manager Marco, CEO Alice -- actor-swiftroute-lena/marco/alice) have no real, seeded QA login. This is ISS-0739's scope; this requirement depends on ISS-0739's resolution to be exercisable end-to-end (AC4 is explicitly deferred to after ISS-0739 lands).

SCOPE: (1) create (or script the creation of) a persistent, live ProcessDefinition for the swiftroute tenant on the QA instance, matching process_route_approval.yaml's graph (name may differ from the fixture's internal filename, but the node/edge/condition shape must match byte-for-byte in behavior); (2) confirm it is reachable and submittable through the ordinary web/ definition-list and instance-submission screens, not only via direct API calls a script makes; (3) explicitly out of scope is inventing new tenant-persona identities in Keycloak -- that is ISS-0739's scope.

NOT IN SCOPE: REQ-396's escalation timer machinery (now done); ISS-0739's credential provisioning; new Keycloak identities.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. A ProcessDefinition matching process_route_approval.yaml's graph exists as a live, active definition for a real tenant on the QA instance -- confirmed by fetching it through the ordinary definitions-list API/screen, not a direct DB query.
2. Submitting an instance with declared_value: 750 against this live definition, via the ordinary API, produces a pending ops-review task followed by a pending ceo-approval task (not an auto-release) -- exercised for real against the QA instance and quoted.
3. Submitting an instance with declared_value: 400 against the same live definition produces no ceo-approval task at all, proving the CEL branch is live, not hardcoded to always route through the CEO.
4. The scenario test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/swiftroute/shipment-high-value-happy.yaml is re-run by UAT-RUNNER once this requirement and ISS-0739 both land, and its own gui-review report is updated from BLOCKED to a real pass/fail verdict with real screenshots. [DEFERRED TO AFTER ISS-0739]
